rationale: Implements the joint selection (groups f833b57a373d8262a384 and 8525af72c631b94e3dd0) at the single shared c10d.allreduce_.default boundary that jointly owns all 13 bucket collectives of the step. Repair of trial-b0a02885e2 using the measured feedback. (1) The concrete failure: every one of the 13 replacement invocations routed parent:guard_reduce_op because the dispatcher passes the reduce op as a torch.ScriptObject wrapping __torch__.torch.classes.c10d.ReduceOp whose op() returns plain integer 0, while torch._C._distributed_c10d.RedOpType is not importable at top level in this worker's torch 2.13.0+cu129 (the enum is nested as type(ReduceOp.SUM)); the P2P exchange therefore never executed and its performance has never been measured. The repaired guard positively identifies SUM from the boxed form only when the script class identity matches the c10d.ReduceOp custom class and the value converts through the RedOpType enum and equals SUM (arbitrary integers are never accepted), verified on the measured worker's Python on CPU: torch.classes.c10d.ReduceOp().op() -> 0, int(ReduceOp.SUM) == 0, type(ReduceOp.SUM)(0) == ReduceOp.SUM. The op's ProcessGroup argument is likewise a ScriptObject and resolves through ProcessGroup.unbox (the form the prior run already passed on its way to the reduce-op guard). (2) The implementation takes the selection hypothesis's explicitly permitted 'equivalent path': instead of host-orchestrated isend/irecv rounds (two host-ordered rounds plus a local add per bucket, whose two-rank gloo rehearsal also showed backend-dependent tag-matching fragility), each flat fp32 bucket's SUM allreduce on the same worker-initialized NCCL process group is decomposed into async reduce_scatter_single(scratch_half, bucket, SUM) followed by async all_gather_single(bucket, scratch_half), both enqueued back-to-back with no host wait between them: NCCL executes collectives issued on one process group in issue order on the group's single device stream, so the allgather is device-ordered after the reduce-scatter, and the returned allgather Work (boxed via work.boxed(), the same return convention torch's own c10d meta registrations use) covers the whole exchange, preserving the parent op's async ABI exactly. Wire volume per rank is unchanged at S bytes, the information-theoretic minimum for an exact allreduce (identical to the ring), and every output element is a single two-addend commutative fp32 add computed on exactly one rank and then copied, so results are bitwise identical across ranks and to the parent SUM; DDP's world-size division happens before this boundary and is untouched. Validated end-to-end on the worker's Python with a CPU/gloo harness at both observed shapes (7,087,872 and 39,385,344 elements, repeated invocations exercising the persistent scratch): results bitwise equal to the parent allreduce op, exact cross-rank equality, parent:guard_size and parent:guard_signature fallbacks executing the parent correctly, and route labels split_allreduce on all supported calls; the gloo branch takes an explicit wait because gloo lacks issue-order execution, while the guarded production path is nccl-only. (3) How the feedback changes this attempt's expectation: the previous candidate was in effect a passthrough ablation - 13 parent calls, byte-identical outputs (max_abs_error 0.0), zero scratch, P2P never run - and still measured 230.5/234.1 ms against parent 131.0/139.1 ms. That +91 to +100 ms is the cost of installing any functional replacement at this unscoped boundary under the legacy binding backend (a global dispatch mode entered for the whole measured invocation, taxing every ATen dispatch of forward, backward and optimizer), and it exceeds the ~62 ms total communication these 13 collectives can influence; even a zero-cost collective cannot recover it, so step_ms improvement is not expected unless that overhead was specific to conditions this bundle changes. This repair makes the selected hypothesis actually executable so the framework's paired AB/BA measurement can decide it on evidence; expected benefit is not acceptance.

setup_work.build_time: No model or parameter transforms, no CUDA work, no new process groups, no comm hooks, no environment changes. build() creates two replacement closures over context['references'] and one per-device scratch cache; installation measured ~4-7 ms in the prior trial and adds no allocation beyond the closure dict.
setup_work.runtime_lazy: The first supported invocation allocates one persistent float32 scratch of numel/2 elements sized for the largest observed bucket (19,692,672 elements = 75.0 MiB for the 39,385,344-element embedding bucket; the 7,087,872-element buckets reuse a prefix slice). The allocation happens once per worker during the first (warmup) invocation and the buffer is retained for the process lifetime, so the caching allocator never races multi-stream reuse; first-use NCCL reduce-scatter/allgather path warmup also lands in warmup invocations.
setup_work.per_call_work: Two async collective enqueues on the process group's NCCL stream (reduce_scatter_single then all_gather_single), no host wait between them on the nccl path, no local add, no chunking, no tags, and a Work.boxed() return. The engine thread is never blocked, matching the parent op's async structure.
setup_work.memory_impact: Steady state retains +75.0 MiB allocated scratch, visible in framework.peak_allocated_bytes and lifecycle counters; no per-invocation growth; no CUDA Graphs or retained graph pools. This is a documented setup/retained allocation, not a general physical-memory saving.

quality_risks: Measured binding overhead dominates: the prior trial's all-parent-fallback execution with byte-identical outputs (max_abs_error 0.0, 13 parent:guard_reduce_op routes) measured 230.5/234.1 ms against parent 131.0/139.1 ms, i.e. ~+95 ms from the legacy functional binding itself (a global dispatch mode active for the whole measured invocation). That exceeds the ~62 ms total communication at these sites, so the paired project measurement will most likely reject this candidate on objective_not_improved unless the overhead was specific to conditions this bundle changes; this is disclosed, not assumed, and acceptance belongs to the framework's AB/BA protocol.

Exactness: every output element is one two-addend commutative fp32 add computed on exactly one rank (the ring reduce-scatter owner of that half) and then copied, so the atol=0/rtol=0 cross-rank replica check holds structurally and values are bitwise equal to the parent SUM; validated bitwise against the parent allreduce op on the worker's Python with a CPU/gloo harness at both observed shapes. DDP's pre-boundary world-size division is untouched, so the reference-gradient (1e-6/1e-4) and post-step parameter checks are unaffected.

The chained async reduce-scatter -> allgather relies on NCCL executing collectives issued on one process group in issue order on the group's single device stream; the CPU/gloo harness lacks that guarantee (it takes an explicit wait and showed corruption without it), so the no-wait branch is production-nccl-only by guard. If the ordering assumption were violated on the worker, gradients would mismatch the single-GPU reference comparison loudly (1e-6/1e-4 per-parameter check) rather than pass silently; a hang would surface as a timeout, never as silent corruption.

The returned Work is the final allgather handle boxed with work.boxed() (the same mechanism torch's own c10d meta registrations use at this op's return position). Because both stages share the process group's NCCL stream and the allgather is enqueued last, its completion covers the entire exchange; DDP-side wait/getFuture on a genuine Work handle is preserved.

Divergent rank routing would hang rather than corrupt: every guard is a pure function of rank-identical inputs (bucket shape/dtype/layout, backend, world membership, reduce op), fallbacks happen strictly before any enqueue, and post-enqueue exceptions propagate instead of triggering a parent fallback (a parent call after a partial exchange would double-reduce the bucket).

The op's timeout argument is not forwarded (the Python collective API accepts no per-call timeout); the process group's default timeout governs both stages, matching the parent's timeout=-1 default behavior.

The workload's second, non-requested diagnostic goal (diagnostic.max_rank_nccl_kernel_sum_ms, measured in separate profiled invocations with a step_ms<=1.05x baseline constraint) counts NCCL AllReduce kernel time; this replacement substitutes ReduceScatter/AllGather kernels, so that diagnostic becomes non-comparable while the requested step_ms objective is unaffected.

Route telemetry: fallback labels distinguish setup failures (parent:setup_process_group, parent:setup_backend, parent:setup_ranks), unsupported signatures (parent:guard_device/dtype/layout/size/backend/world_size/reduce_op/sparse_indices/tensor_list/signature, parent:error_<Type> for pre-enqueue exceptions) and the executed path (split_allreduce); labels are diagnostic self-report only.
Retained +75.0 MiB scratch raises warm-run peak_allocated_bytes and lifecycle counters; reported explicitly rather than described as a saving.
